title: Token bucket for driver location pings
name: Driver ping limiter

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code throttles location pings per driver? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is none. Refill is capped at burst with Math.min, so idle drivers cannot bank unlimited tokens; elapsed time is clamped at 0 and uses performance.now(), a monotonic clock, so wall-clock adjustments cannot mint tokens; the timestamp is updated on both allow and deny paths without losing fractional tokens because the stored value is the already-refilled amount; and waitMs is computed from the actual deficit. Per-driver state is removed when the driver goes offline, so the Map does not grow with churn.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A new driver sends 5 pings in the same millisecond. How many are accepted?
choices: 0, because the first ping has no prior state
choiceQuestions.explanation: With no prior state, available starts at burst (3). Each allowed ping stores available - 1, and with zero elapsed time no refill happens, so pings 1-3 pass (3, 2, 1 available) and pings 4 and 5 see 0 and are denied. Missing state means a full bucket, not an empty one.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Right after its bucket empties, a driver is denied. It retries every 100 ms. What happens to its retries?
choices: Each denied retry resets the refill, so it is locked out indefinitely
The first retry after about 1 second is accepted
Retries are accepted immediately because denial stores no state
It must wait burst / ratePerSec = 3 seconds
choiceQuestions.explanation: On denial the limiter stores the refilled amount with the new timestamp, so accumulated fractions are kept (0.1 per 100 ms). After about 1 s available reaches 1 and the ping is allowed. Denials do not reset progress, they do write state, and only one token (not a full burst) is needed.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Pings with lat = 200 arrive rapidly from one driver. How do they interact with the limiter?
choices: They consume tokens and then get 400
They get 429 once the bucket empties
They are rejected with 400 before the limiter is consulted and consume no tokens
They are clamped to 90 and accepted
choiceQuestions.explanation: onPing validates coordinates first and returns 400 before calling limiter.allow, so invalid pings never touch the bucket and never see 429. Nothing clamps values. This means invalid traffic is not throttled by this limiter, a tradeoff that keeps bad payloads from eating a driver's budget.
